back2basics.text: Satellite navigation systems use a constellation of satellites to provide autonomous geo-spatial positioning. These systems transmit signals that receivers use to determine location and time information. Indigenous systems like NavIC provide regional navigation services tailored to national needs, enhancing strategic autonomy and civilian applications.

body.label: Next-generation satellite
body.text: NVS-03 is the third satellite of the second-generation Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC) series, designed to augment and support continuity of India's regional navigation services.

body.label: Enhanced capabilities
body.text: It carries an indigenous Rubidium atomic clock and transmits signals in L1, L5, and S bands, with the L1 band ensuring compatibility with modern civilian smartphone chipsets and wearable devices.

body.label: Strategic importance
body.text: NVS-03 advances India's pursuit of self-reliance in critical satellite navigation technologies, strengthening navigation services for citizens.

sections.heading: What is the NVS-03 satellite and its significance?

body.label: Launch vehicle details
body.text: The satellite was launched aboard the 50-metre-tall, three-stage Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV-F18) with a lift-off mass of 420 tonnes from Satish Dhawan Space Centre.

body.label: Orbit specifics
body.text: NVS-03 was deployed into a Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit with a perigee of 170 km, an apogee of 37,023 km, and an inclination of 20.75 degrees before orbit-raising manoeuvres to its final geosynchronous slot at 32.5 degrees East.

body.label: Engineering innovation
body.text: ISRO flew the satellite with pyrotechnic valves open during liftoff, a departure from standard protocols, to avoid connector failures experienced in the previous NVS-02 mission.

body.label: Safety enhancements
body.text: Corrective measures recommended by a high-level committee were integrated to improve redundancy and pyro system operations for mission success.

sections.heading: How was the NVS-03 satellite launched and what were the technical features?

body.label: Strengthening NavIC
body.text: The launch is a crucial step in restoring and strengthening India's indigenous regional satellite navigation system, NavIC.

body.label: Self-reliance in technology
body.text: It reflects India's advancement in critical technologies like atomic clocks and satellite navigation, contributing to technological self-reliance.

body.label: Strategic and civilian benefits
body.text: Improved navigation services benefit both strategic applications and civilian users, including smartphone and wearable device compatibility.

back2basics.text: FTAs are treaties between countries that reduce or eliminate tariffs, import quotas, and preferences on goods and services traded between the signatories. They aim to increase trade and economic integration by providing preferential market access and addressing issues like rules of origin, intellectual property, and investment protections. FTAs can also include cooperation on technology, services, and regulatory standards, helping countries leverage their comparative advantages and foster economic growth.

back2basics.concept: Price Hike and Its Economic Impact
back2basics.text: A price hike is an increase in the selling price of a commodity, often to cover rising input costs or to support producers. While it can help producers earn better income, it may also increase the financial burden on consumers and contribute to inflation. Governments must balance these effects when setting prices for essential goods like milk.

2026-10-31-pm-93167a232e.deck: Karnataka government raised milk prices by ₹8 to support dairy farmers amid rising input costs. back2basics.text: Poverty is commonly measured by income thresholds such as the international poverty lines defined by the World Bank, including extreme poverty at $3.00/day and lower middle-income poverty at $4.20/day. Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) measures poverty beyond income, considering factors like education, health, and living standards to capture non-monetary deprivation.

body.label: Monetary poverty decline
body.text: Between 2011 and 2023, the share of the population living below the Lower Middle-Income Country line ($4.2/day) fell from 57.7% to 16.1%, lifting an estimated 496 million people out of poverty.

body.label: Extreme poverty reduction

body.label: Non-monetary poverty improvement

sections.heading: What progress has India made in reducing poverty?

body.label: Employment growth
body.text: Employment increased by about 134 million people between 2017 and 2023, nearly twice the growth of the working-age population, with rural women accounting for much of this gain.

body.label: Social transfers and subsidies
body.text: Expanded social transfers, including food subsidies, played a significant role in reducing poverty.

body.label: Improved consumption and welfare
body.text: Strong consumption growth and welfare gains were observed in both rural and urban households, with rural India narrowing the rural-urban welfare gap.

body.label: Infrastructure access
body.text: Access to electricity reached 99% of the population by 2022, supporting improved living standards.

sections.heading: What factors contributed to this poverty reduction?

body.label: Concentration of poverty
body.text: Poverty is increasingly concentrated among households with lower education, fewer assets, limited stable employment, and higher dependency ratios.

body.label: Geographical concentration
body.text: About 57% of India's poor population live in a contiguous belt from Uttar Pradesh to West Bengal.

body.label: Wage disparities
body.text: Median earnings among the top 10% of workers were about 13 times those of the bottom 10% in 2023.

body.label: Youth unemployment
body.text: Youth unemployment rose from 14.6% to 15.9% between Q1 FY2026 and Q1 FY2027, particularly among rural young women.

body.label: Employment quality
body.text: Real earnings remained broadly unchanged as employment growth was concentrated in relatively low-productivity activities.

back2basics.text: Electoral rolls are periodically revised to remove names of ineligible voters such as those who have died, moved away, or are duplicates. The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) is a process conducted by the Election Commission to update and clean voter lists to ensure accuracy. However, this process must balance removing ineligible names with protecting eligible voters from wrongful exclusion, as voter rolls are fundamental to free and fair elections.

2026-10-31-pm-d0e855890a.deck: The Election Commission of India’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Karnataka led to the exclusion of 6,58,862 voters, about 15.8% of Belagavi district’s electorate. This raises concerns about electoral integrity and voter disenfranchisement ahead of elections.

body.label: Voter exclusion scale
body.text: Belagavi district’s electoral rolls shrank from 41,53,775 voters in January 2025 to 34,94,913 after the SIR, excluding 6,58,862 voters or 15.8% of the electorate.

body.label: Comparison with other regions
body.text: The deletion percentage in Belagavi is higher than Karnataka’s average of 12% but lower than Bengaluru’s 43% deletion rate.

body.label: Muslim voter impact
body.text: Among the excluded voters, approximately 1,03,839 were Muslims, with significant deletions in constituencies like Belgaum Uttar and Kudachi.

sections.heading: What happened during the Special Intensive Revision in Belagavi?

body.label: Effect on electoral outcomes
body.text: In several constituencies, the number of deleted voters far exceeds the winning margins of elected representatives, potentially affecting election results.

body.label: Allegations of misuse
body.text: Complaints were made about violations of Form 7 application rules, including document fudging and intimidation, suggesting possible manipulation of the voter deletion process.

body.label: Voter disenfranchisement
body.text: Large-scale deletions, especially of minority voters, raise concerns about disenfranchisement and the fairness of the electoral process.

sections.heading: Why does this voter exclusion matter for elections and democracy?

body.label: Categories of deletions
body.text: Deletions included Absent, Shifted, Dead, Duplicate and Others (ASDDO), pre-SIR deletions, and those based on third-party objections via Form 7 applications.

body.label: Role of Form 7 objections
body.text: Many deletions resulted from third-party objections filed under Form 7, some of which were later withdrawn, admitting misuse of the process.

body.label: Political and legal responses
body.text: Affected leaders and parties lodged complaints with the Election Commission and law enforcement, highlighting irregularities and seeking redress.

back2basics.text: The Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) is a constitutional authority responsible for conducting free and fair elections in India. The CEC enjoys independence to ensure impartiality. Impeachment or removal of the CEC is a rare and serious process that involves parliamentary procedures to maintain checks and balances in democracy. Understanding these provisions helps grasp how constitutional bodies are held accountable.

sections.heading: What is the INDIA bloc's public impeachment event about?

body.label: Avoiding parliamentary mockery
body.text: The event will avoid impersonations, posters, or banners depicting the Prime Minister, Home Minister, or CEC to prevent mocking Parliament.

body.label: Speaking time allocation
body.text: Leaders of the Opposition in both Houses will get about 20 minutes each, while other parties will get 5 to 10 minutes to speak.

body.label: Supervision
body.text: Priyanka Gandhi Vadra is supervising the event's finer details.

sections.heading: How will the public impeachment be conducted?

body.label: Constitutional oversight
body.text: The event raises questions on the constitutional provisions and parliamentary procedures related to the impeachment and accountability of the Chief Election Commissioner.

body.label: Role of Election Commission
body.text: Understanding the Election Commission's role and its independence is crucial for governance and polity topics in UPSC.

body.label: Political accountability
body.text: The public impeachment reflects political mechanisms to hold constitutional authorities accountable, relevant for mains answers on democratic governance.
